query: For bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified predictive approach make to overcome the limited accuracy of available analytical predictions and their usual restriction to perfect, defect-free crystals? Address the nearly 0–200 K regime and the 300–1200 K regime, for which measurements also exist on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen; explain why the approach should improve accuracy, predict its advantage over existing analytical approaches, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a held-out conductivity benchmark and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A physics-informed machine-learning (PIML) model that explicitly incorporates mass/strain-field disorder and oxygen-interstitial scattering can predict the lattice thermal conductivity κ of bulk equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr to within ±10 % of experiment from 5 K to 1200 K, whereas state-of-the-art analytical models (e.g., Debye–Callaway, Slack, and effective-medium formalisms developed for ordered crystals) incur ≥25 % error and systematically under-predict κ below 200 K and over-predict it above 800 K.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk polycrystalline equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy; two cases: (i) high-purity (<0.05 wt.% O) for 5–200 K tests, (ii) same alloy containing 1 wt.% O for 300–1200 K tests; grains ≈50–100 µm; fully recrystallised bcc solid solution; ρ ≈ 7.8 g cm⁻³.
generation.intervention: Apply a PIML thermal-transport predictor trained on high-fidelity DFT and molecular-dynamics data sets that sample (a) random chemical disorder configurations, (b) point-defect scattering by oxygen interstitials up to 1 wt.%, and (c) phonon–electron coupling at elevated temperatures.
generation.conditions: Steady-state or laser-flash measurements under high vacuum; temperature windows 5–200 K (oxygen-lean sample) and 300–1200 K (1 wt.% O sample); negligible external stress; no phase transformation (confirmed by in-situ XRD).
generation.structural_mediator: Phonon mean-free-path spectrum modified by (1) mass and strain-field fluctuations from equiatomic disorder and (2) resonant scattering from interstitial oxygen; both explicitly parameterised in the PIML feature set.
generation.mechanism: By learning the energy-dependent phonon scattering rates from thousands of ab-initio and MD snapshots that embed realistic disorder and impurity configurations, the PIML model reconstructs the full phonon Boltzmann transport equation solution without assuming a perfect crystal. Consequently, it captures short-range disorder and defect scattering that dominate κ in HfNbTaTiZr, especially at low T (Rayleigh regime) and high T (Umklapp + impurity regime).
generation.predicted_outcome: Mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of the PIML predictions for κ(T) ≤10 % across both temperature regimes, with maximum pointwise error ≤15 %. Analytical models will show MAPE ≥25 % and cross the experimental curve by ≥30 % near 50 K and >800 K.
generation.baseline: Best-available analytical predictions for defect-free bcc crystals using Debye–Callaway with averaged mass and elastic constants, omitting explicit disorder and oxygen scattering.
generation.boundary: Prediction expected to hold only for (1) oxygen content ≤1 wt.%, (2) temperatures ≤1200 K (below incipient phase separation/oxidation), and (3) grain sizes ≥10 µm (to minimise grain-boundary scattering not in the model). Extrapolations outside these limits are not claimed.
generation.uncertainty: Model quality depends on the breadth of training data; unrepresented longer-range clustering or unforeseen precipitates above ~1000 K could increase errors. Experimental uncertainties (±5 %) may conflate evaluation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two specimens: (A) O-lean and (B) 1 wt.% O alloy, both fully recrystallised. Measure κ(T) every 25 K from 5 K to 200 K for A and from 300 K to 1200 K for B using laser-flash analysis with density and heat-capacity corrections. Blind the PIML model to these data, then predict κ(T) for each point.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If at any measured temperature the absolute prediction error |κ_pred−κ_exp| exceeds 15 %, or if overall MAPE exceeds 10 %, the hypothesis is falsified.
